question: In 2002-2003, the Government of India set up a committee to review the fiscal reforms both in respect of Direct and Indirect taxes under the chairmanship of ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijay Kelkar**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• In **2002-2003**, the **Government of India** established a committee to review fiscal reforms in both **Direct and Indirect taxes**. 
• The committee was chaired by **Vijay Kelkar**, a renowned economist and policy advisor. 
• The primary objective of this committee was to provide recommendations for **tax simplification**, improving **tax compliance**, and enhancing **economic growth** through efficient fiscal policy. 
• The committee submitted its report, known as the **Kelkar Committee Report**, which highlighted several reforms to improve the **tax structure** in India. 
• It emphasized the need for a more **transparent and effective tax system** to promote economic development and reduce administrative burdens. 
• The **Kelkar Committee** played a pivotal role in shaping India's fiscal policies and provided a roadmap for future reforms in taxation.
